messages:
Alice: Morning — quick async standup.
Alice: Yesterday: finished the rate-policy unit tests for prefix routing, fixed an edge case where fallback rules ignored auth-headers.
Alice: Blockers: still seeing intermittent 429s in staging during burst tests; not sure if it's batching or the token bucket settings.
Alice: Today: will iterate on rate-policy defaults and open a tiny PR for config tuning.

Ben: Thanks Alice. I saw the 429s too during the 2pm load-run.
Ben: Repro steps were low concurrency with short bursts — looks like many small requests causing batch windows to misfire.
Ben: I can try increasing the batching window by 10ms and re-run.

Carlos: ping me on the PR, happy to review. Quick question: are these 429s coming from the auth layer (jwt middleware) or from the gw rate limiter?

Alice: Good q — logs point to gw limiter rejecting after auth success. snippet from the log:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z gw-1 rate_limiter.cpp:312 WARN token_bucket=0 user_id=svc-123 request=/v1/complete
```

Dana: FYI I bumped the metric granularity in staging so you should see per-route token usage in the console now.
Dana: Also added a short-lived dashboard for the test run. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Evan: For the config change, consider adding a per-route burst allowance for small payload endpoints (embeddings, health).
Evan: Example snippet we used before: 
```json
{"route": "/v1/embeddings", "rate_limit": {"window_ms": 1000, "requests": 50, "burst": 25}}
```

Ben: I raised a PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/842 — changes batching window + adds an opt-in per-route burst flag.
Ben: @Dana @Carlos can you take a quick look when free?

Carlos: ACK, will review after standup.

Dana: Quick nudge — deployment slot for this is in the 4pm canary. If tests pass, we can promote.

Alice: I'll attach the failing trace to the PR so reviewers have context.
Alice: Also adding a tiny e2e that simulates many short requests to catch this earlier.

Evan: One more ask: can we add a short doc blurb about when to use per-route bursts vs global quotas? Saves future churn.

Ben: +1, I'll add a docs note under /docs/rate-limits.md in the PR branch.

DeployBot: Canary deploy scheduled: gateway:v2.14.3 -> staging (us-west-2) at 16:05 UTC. Monitor: /dash/gw-staging/canary.

Alice: Great — I'll watch the metrics and ping here.
Alice: If the 429s disappear with the batching tweak, we'll promote; if not, next step is to inspect kernel-level scheduling (gpu inference batching) which might interact with request shaping.

Carlos: Sounds good. Catch up in the thread if anything pops.
Carlos: :thumbsup:

Dana: No blockers from infra side.
Dana: Leaving the dashboard links in the PR comments.

Evan: Thanks all, small follow-ups queued.

Ben: Thanks — will notify when canary traffic completes.

DeployBot: Canary completed: 10k requests passed, 0 regressions detected, promote ready.

Alice: Promoted to blue by me. :rocket:
Alice: Closing the loop — observed 3x fewer 429s in the burst test after batching window increase. Will keep the per-route burst opt-in for a week and then propose defaults.
